title: [v0.91.8][runtime-v3][observability] Integrate tracing with Vector durable master logging
body:
## Summary

Implement one production Runtime v3 logging path using the existing Rust `tracing` facade and the pinned Vector component. Vector must own collection, durable file output, redaction, buffering, routing, and OTLP delivery. Do not add a custom logging facade, custom rotation system, Python wrapper, or parallel general-purpose JSONL logger.

## Problem

Runtime v3 emits some `tracing` events but production does not install a complete subscriber and collector path. The WP-12 lifecycle harness needs a durable, high-throughput master log whose contents can be audited after 10,000 lifecycle cycles, 100 independent 10-second stress windows, and 10 independent 10-minute endurance windows on macOS, Linux/EC2, and native Windows/Nessus. Every error, panic, guardian exit, restart, shutdown, adapter failure, continuity failure, and observability-pipeline failure must be attributable.

## Scope

- Install a production `tracing-subscriber` JSON ingress for Runtime v3.
- Feed that ingress into one long-lived pinned Vector process per runtime/suite.
- Make Vector write the canonical durable master log and retain existing OTLP/CloudWatch routing capabilities.
- Preserve the complete Runtime v2 OTEL behavior: OTLP/HTTP export, ADL and standard endpoint/timeout configuration, service resource attributes, command/stage/result attributes, trace/span/parent IDs, severity and span status, exporter monitor status, runtime API status/log exposure, service-environment propagation, and durable sink/export failure reporting when stderr is suppressed.
- Preserve stdout/stderr machine/human channel contracts.
- Include stable event fields: timestamp, severity, target, runtime instance, guardian identity, process identity, lifecycle/run/cycle correlation, component/adapter, operation, reason code, error chain, and exact revision when available.
- Redact secrets before durable or remote egress.
- Flush/drain cleanly on guardian-owned shutdown and report incomplete drain as a failure.
- Detect Vector death, restart it under existing supervision, and record the causal exit/restart without silently losing audit events.
- Add a deterministic log auditor that rejects malformed JSON, sequence gaps, missing required fields, panic/error/degraded markers in successful runs, unexplained restarts, pipeline health failures, and incomplete drain.
- Prove the same behavior on macOS, Linux/EC2, and native Windows/Nessus.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Production Runtime v3 installs `tracing` once and emits structured events into Vector; no runtime event is silently discarded because no subscriber exists.
2. Vector is the only general log writer/router. No custom logging facade, custom rotation implementation, Python server/wrapper, or second master-log implementation is introduced.
3. A canonical append-only master log is produced under an explicit absolute configured state root with documented retention/rotation owned by Vector.
4. Errors include causal context sufficient to identify the failing runtime instance, guardian process, child process, adapter/component, operation, reason code, and correlated lifecycle window.
5. Secrets and credentials are redacted before durable and remote output, with adversarial regression coverage.
6. Normal shutdown drains and flushes the pipeline; crash/restart behavior is observable and bounded. Missing Vector or failed Vector startup fails closed rather than claiming healthy/degraded success.
7. Runtime v3 retains full Runtime v2 OTEL parity: OTLP/HTTP export; `ADL_OTEL_EXPORTER_*` and standard `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*` endpoint/timeout configuration; `service.name` resource identity; command, stage, result, and governed correlation attributes; trace, span, and parent-span propagation; severity/status mapping; exporter health and last-event status; runtime API consumption; service-manager environment propagation; and durable export-failure evidence even with stderr suppressed.
8. Vector exports real OTLP logs, traces, and metrics with bounded batching, retry/backoff, disk buffering for audit signals, endpoint health checks, and acknowledged delivery. Local durable output remains authoritative when remote delivery is unavailable; health must distinguish local durability from remote export health without claiming degraded production success.
9. The clean-log auditor fails on any malformed record, sequence gap, hash/correlation mismatch, unexplained restart, panic, error, degraded/unavailable state, or incomplete drain.
10. WP-12 can consume the canonical Vector master log for 10,000 start/stop cycles, 100x10-second stress, and 10x10-minute endurance acceptance without a custom harness log writer.
11. Focused tests, strict Clippy, exact-head review, and native macOS/Linux/Windows proof pass.

## Non-Goals

- No legacy Runtime v1 deletion.
- No observatory HTML/UI work.
- No replacement for Vector, `tracing`, rustls, Axum, or Tokio.
- No fixture-only, receipt-only, simulated, degraded, or metadata-only acceptance credit.

## Validation

Use focused Rust tests and a real pinned Vector binary. Compare Runtime v3 against the retained Runtime v2 OTEL tests and service/runtime API surfaces, then prove real local Vector output plus a bounded authenticated OTLP receiver exchange. All retained evidence and generated logs must live under the issue worktree or its configured remote checkout, never `/private/tmp`.
